items.q: I worked with him in Chicago.

ctx.x: I worked with him in Chicago.
Oh, you were up in Chicago?

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-04-04
items.q: The first one I saw did was Frederick Keppigan and I first went to Chicago.

ctx.x: Well, I did that a lot. Tell me that comes from King Oliver. Tell me King Oliver first one did that.
He was strong, you know, and he put them valves half down, he didn't make any more of anything. The first one I saw did was Frederick Keppigan and I first went to Chicago. Did Buddy Petit do that?

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1959-09-01
items.q: I worked with Freddy Keppert at the Dream Land.

ctx.x: The district. Oh hell yeah man. You was. I was playing with a fellow and Ken Beard in the daytime. Cans of the women, you know, the whole hustle of them. 10 cents a can and every night I'd get up there and play the blues with the piano player. Now he, I forget his name, he died. He was a sickly fellow but he died. But I, nothing but blues all night. I'd sit up and play the blues all night. A fellow named Tootlum. Tootlum. Gravity and Gravy. All right let me ask you this. It's known that Jelly Roll played here in…
Which band was it that Keppert was in you were in?

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1959-09-25
items.q: But I played with Freddie, you know.

ctx.x: Was there any of the guys playing like Freddie Caput down here?

Well, no. But I played with Freddie, you know. That's something I forgot to tell you. Now that was a trumpet player in the band. See, I went to that dream and there were so many different fellows, but now I went there with Freddie Caput. But how it happened, it wasn't tying the band to Freddie Caput band. Oh yeah. But I went there with him.
Who was in the band with Freddie?
